## Purpose

This SOP describes the operation, calibration verification, and
maintenance of SonTek acoustic Doppler velocity meters used for point
velocity and discharge measurements in wadeable streams. Acoustic
Doppler instruments measure water velocity by transmitting ultrasonic
pulses and detecting the frequency shift of sound reflected by
suspended particles in the water column [@rehmel2007]. Unlike
mechanical current meters ([SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd)),
acoustic meters have no moving parts, respond faster to turbulent
fluctuations, and can measure very low velocities.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** SonTek FlowTracker2 and FlowTracker (original model)
  handheld acoustic Doppler velocimeters (ADVs) used for wading
  discharge measurements in streams and channels
- **Does not apply to:** SonTek ADP/ADCP profiling instruments for
  non-wadeable rivers or boat-mounted surveys; mechanical current
  meters (see [SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd));
  fixed-installation acoustic flow meters in pipes or culverts
- **Location:** All EA Program wadeable stream sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve instrument deployment; ensure firmware is current |
| Trained Personnel | Operate instrument per this SOP; download and archive data |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **ADV (acoustic Doppler velocimeter):** An instrument that measures
  water velocity at a single point by transmitting ultrasonic pulses
  and measuring the Doppler frequency shift of sound scattered back
  from suspended particles in a small sampling volume located at a
  fixed distance from the transducer head [@rehmel2007].
- **Averaging time:** The duration over which velocity samples are
  collected and averaged at each measurement vertical; the FlowTracker
  default is 40 seconds; increase to 60 seconds in low-velocity or
  highly turbulent flows to improve measurement stability [@sontek_ft2].
- **Beam check:** A pre-measurement quality check in which the
  FlowTracker2 tests all three acoustic beams and reports signal-to-
  noise ratio (SNR) for each; all beams must return SNR > 4 dB before
  a measurement can proceed [@sontek_ft2].
- **Boundary flag:** An automated QC flag set by the FlowTracker when
  the probe is too close to the streambed or water surface for the
  sampling volume to be fully within the water column; corrected by
  adjusting the depth setting.
- **Doppler effect:** The change in frequency of a wave (sound or
  light) observed when the source or the reflector is in motion
  relative to the observer; the physical basis of acoustic Doppler
  velocity measurement -- the frequency shift of reflected ultrasound
  is proportional to the component of particle velocity along the
  acoustic beam axis [@rehmel2007].
- **FlowTracker2:** The current production SonTek handheld ADV for
  wading discharge measurements; uses three acoustic beams and
  integrated pressure depth sensor; stores data internally and
  transfers via USB; includes automated QA/QC flagging [@sontek_ft2].
- **Mid-section method:** The standard USGS discharge calculation
  method in which each vertical's discharge is the product of measured
  velocity, depth, and the horizontal width extending halfway to the
  adjacent verticals on each side; computed automatically by the
  FlowTracker [@turnipseed2010].
- **MMT file:** The proprietary binary data file format produced by
  the SonTek FlowTracker; stores raw velocity data, QC flags, site
  information, and the computed discharge summary; must be archived
  before exporting to CSV.
- **Sampling volume:** The small water volume approximately 10 cm from
  the FlowTracker transducer head from which velocity data are
  collected; must be free of boundary interference (streambed, water
  surface, or large obstacles) for valid measurements [@sontek_ft2].
- **SNR (signal-to-noise ratio):** The ratio of acoustic signal
  strength returned from suspended particles to background noise;
  expressed in dB; the FlowTracker requires SNR > 4 dB on all three
  beams for a valid measurement; low SNR typically indicates
  insufficient suspended particles in very clear water [@sontek_ft2].
- **Spike flag:** An automated QC flag set by the FlowTracker when a
  single velocity sample deviates significantly from the running mean,
  indicating a transient disturbance (bubble, debris, wading
  disturbance); the affected sample is excluded from the average.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Wading in flowing water carries drowning risk. Always
  work in pairs. Do not wade in flows deeper than waist height or
  where footing is unstable.
- **Electrical:** The FlowTracker uses internal rechargeable batteries.
  Do not open the sealed housing in the field.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens; decontaminate equipment between
  sites per [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd).
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Chest or hip waders with felt or studded soles
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

A minimum of two people must be present for all in-stream work. Refer
to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general
emergency procedures.


## Instrument Specifications

### FlowTracker2

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Measurement principle  | Acoustic Doppler velocimetry (ADV)         |
| Velocity range         | 0.001--4.0 m/s (0.003--13 ft/s)           |
| Velocity accuracy      | ±1% of measured velocity                  |
| Velocity resolution    | 0.0001 m/s                                 |
| Sampling volume        | Located 10 cm from the transducer          |
| Depth sensor           | Integrated pressure sensor, 0--5 m range  |
| Data storage           | Internal memory; USB download              |
| Battery                | Rechargeable lithium-ion; ~12 hr continuous |
| QC diagnostics         | Automated QA/QC (SNR, boundary, flow angle, spike detection) |

[@sontek_ft2]

### FlowTracker (Original)

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Measurement principle  | Acoustic Doppler velocimetry (ADV)         |
| Velocity range         | 0.001--4.5 m/s                             |
| Velocity accuracy      | ±1% of measured velocity                  |
| Sampling volume        | Located 10 cm from the transducer          |
| Data storage           | Internal memory; RS-232 download           |
| Battery                | 3 C-cell alkaline batteries                |


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| SonTek FlowTracker2 (or original)     | Charged and firmware updated [@sontek_ft2] |
| Top-setting wading rod                | Standard USGS-type; FlowTracker mounts on the rod |
| Mounting bracket and thumbscrew       | Specific to SonTek; included with instrument |
| USB cable                             | For data download (FlowTracker2)         |
| RS-232 cable and adapter (original model) | For data download                    |
| Measuring tape (50 m)                 | For establishing the tag line            |
| Tape stakes (2)                       | For anchoring the tag line               |
| Laptop or tablet with SonTek software | FlowTracker2 uses SonTek's desktop software |
| Field data sheet (backup)             | Printed on waterproof paper              |
| Spare batteries                       | C-cells for original model               |


## Procedure

### Pre-Field Setup

1. Charge the FlowTracker2 battery fully before each field day
   [@sontek_ft2]. For the original model, install fresh batteries.
2. Power on the instrument and verify that the firmware version is
   current. Update if prompted.
3. Set the site information: site name, station ID, date, and operator
   initials.
4. Select the measurement method:
   - **Mid-section** (default, consistent with USGS practice
     [@turnipseed2010])
   - **Mean-section** (if required by the project)
5. Set the measurement parameters:
   - Averaging time: 40 seconds (default; increase to 60 seconds for
     low or turbulent flows) [@sontek_ft2]
   - Number of measurements per vertical: 1 (six-tenths method) or 2
     (two-point method at 0.2 and 0.8 depth) [@turnipseed2010]

### Beam Check

Perform a beam check before each measurement [@sontek_ft2].

1. Submerge the probe head at least 15 cm below the water surface in
   a location with minimal turbulence.
2. On the FlowTracker2, select **QC > Beam Check** from the menu.
3. The instrument tests all three acoustic beams and reports SNR for
   each beam.
4. All beams must report SNR > 4 dB. If any beam fails, clean the
   transducer faces and retest. If the beam check still fails, do not
   proceed with the measurement.
5. Record the beam check result in the field notebook.

### Site Selection and Tag Line

Follow the site selection and tag line procedures described in
[SOP-F301 Stream Discharge Measurement](SOP-F301-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd),
Sections 7.1--7.3 [@turnipseed2010]. The same cross-section criteria
apply to acoustic and mechanical meters.

### Making the Measurement

1. Mount the FlowTracker probe on the wading rod at the correct depth
   setting:
   - **Six-tenths method:** Set the probe at 0.6 of the total depth
     below the water surface (same as for mechanical meters)
   - **Two-point method:** Measure at 0.2 and 0.8 of the depth
2. At each vertical, the instrument automatically records velocity
   (Vx, Vy components) and runs QC checks (SNR, spike detection,
   boundary check, flow angle).
3. If a measurement is flagged, the instrument displays the reason.
   Common flags and responses:

| Flag               | Meaning                              | Response                          |
|:-------------------|:-------------------------------------|:----------------------------------|
| Low SNR            | Insufficient suspended particles     | Increase averaging time; stir bed gently upstream |
| Boundary           | Probe too close to bed or surface     | Adjust depth setting              |
| High flow angle    | Flow not perpendicular to tag line    | Reposition tag line or note angle |
| Spike              | Velocity spike detected              | Repeat measurement                |

[@sontek_ft2]

4. After completing all verticals, the instrument computes total
   discharge automatically using the mid-section method [@turnipseed2010].
5. Review the on-screen discharge summary before leaving the site.

### Post-Measurement

1. Save the measurement file on the instrument.
2. Record a backup note in the field notebook: site, date, total
   discharge, number of verticals, and any flagged stations.
3. Rinse the probe with clean water. Do not use solvents or abrasives
   on the transducer faces.
4. Decontaminate per [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd)
   before moving to the next site.

### Data Download

1. Connect the FlowTracker2 to a laptop via USB.
2. Open the SonTek desktop software and download all measurement files
   [@sontek_ft2].
3. Export each measurement as a `.csv` and a `.dis` (discharge summary)
   file.
4. Save files using the naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_discharge_FT2.csv`
5. Upload to the project GitHub repository under `data/discharge/`
   within 48 hours.
6. Archive the raw `.mmt` file to the lab shared drive.


## Maintenance

### After Each Field Day

1. Rinse the entire probe head and cable with clean fresh water.
2. Dry with a lint-free cloth.
3. Inspect the transducer faces for scratches, algae buildup, or
   debris. Clean gently with a soft brush if needed.
4. Charge the battery (FlowTracker2) or remove batteries (original
   model) if storing for more than one week.

### Periodic Maintenance

- **Monthly (active use):** Inspect the wading rod mounting bracket
  for wear. Verify firmware version.
- **Annually:** Contact SonTek for factory calibration verification if
  the instrument is used for regulatory or compliance monitoring
  [@rehmel2007].


## Quality Control

- Beam check before every measurement (§7.2) [@sontek_ft2].
- If two measurements are made at the same cross-section, they should
  agree within 5%; if they differ by more than 5%, make a third
  measurement and use the mean of the two closest values
  [@turnipseed2010].
- Compare FlowTracker results with mechanical meter results at least
  once per year; results should agree within 5--8% [@rehmel2007].
- Review all automated QC flags during data processing. Do not discard
  flagged data without documentation.

## Training Record

Before using SonTek velocity meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F301](SOP-F301-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd) in full
2. Complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Observe a trained operator perform a complete discharge measurement
   including beam check, measurement, and data download
4. Perform a supervised discharge measurement with results that agree
   within 5% of the trainer's independent measurement
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
